target: Jag äter lunch med kollegorna.
english: I eat lunch with the colleagues.
tip: Kollega pluralizes to kollegor, then kollegorna for the colleagues.

target: En enkelbiljett till Göteborg, tack.
english: A one-way ticket to Gothenburg, please.
tip: Enkelbiljett is a one-way ticket, from enkel (single); a return is tur och retur.

target: Han lämnar barnen på dagis.
english: He drops the children off at daycare.
tip: Dagis is the everyday word for daycare: lämnar barnen på dagis = drops the kids at daycare.

target: Jag åker Öresundståget till Köpenhamn.
english: I take the Öresund train to Copenhagen.
tip: Åka is the go-by-vehicle verb: åker Öresundståget = take the Öresund train.

target: Jag vill lära mig mer svenska.
english: I want to learn more Swedish.
tip: Vill means 'want', not English 'will': jag vill lära mig means I want to learn, not I will learn.

target: Hon dricker te istället för kaffe.
english: She drinks tea instead of coffee.
tip: Istället för is the fixed phrase for instead of: te istället för kaffe.

target: Vi tränar tre gånger i veckan.
english: We exercise three times a week.
tip: Frequency uses gånger plus i veckan: tre gånger i veckan = three times a week.

target: I morse åt vi frukost tidigt.
english: This morning we ate breakfast early.
tip: i morse = earlier this morning (already past); don't mix it up with i morgon = tomorrow.

target: Han hjälper sina grannar med trädgårdsarbete.
english: He helps his neighbors with garden work.
tip: Sina is the plural of reflexive sin, pointing back to the subject: hjälper sina grannar.

target: Barnen läser böcker innan de somnar.
english: The children read books before they fall asleep.
tip: Somna means fall asleep (the change), while sova means be asleep: innan de somnar.

target: Det är mitt första besök i Sverige.
english: It is my first visit to Sweden.
tip: Possessives agree with the noun: neuter besök takes mitt, so mitt första besök.

target: Mannen som bor här är min granne.
english: The man who lives here is my neighbor.
tip: "Som" is the all-purpose relative pronoun – it replaces who, which, that.

target: Barnet som leker i parken är glatt.
english: The child playing in the park is happy.
tip: Predicate adjectives agree too: neuter barnet makes glad become glatt, so Barnet är glatt.

target: God kväll allihopa, välkomna till vår lilla fest.
english: Good evening everyone, welcome to our little party.
tip: Liten is wildly irregular: definite lilla, plural små. Here vår lilla fest = our little party.

target: Hon sjunger vackert och spelar piano varje eftermiddag.
english: She sings beautifully and plays piano every afternoon.
tip: Make an adverb by adding -t: vacker becomes vackert, so sjunger vackert = sings beautifully.

target: I Sverige äter man ofta middag vid sex.
english: In Sweden one often eats dinner at six.
tip: Swedish keeps the verb in second place, so fronting I Sverige puts äter ahead of the subject man: I Sverige äter man.

target: De studerar ekonomi vid Lunds universitet sedan hösten.
english: They have been studying economics at Lund University since autumn.
tip: Swedish keeps the present with sedan for an ongoing action: studerar sedan hösten = have studied since autumn.

target: Dessutom är maten billigare i den andra butiken.
english: Besides, the food is cheaper in the other store.
tip: A definite noun with an adjective needs a front article too: den andra butiken = the other shop.

target: En läkare undersökte patienten noggrant på sjukhuset igår.
english: A doctor examined the patient carefully at the hospital yesterday.
tip: Group-2 verbs form the past with -te or -de: undersöker becomes undersökte = examined.

target: Nu måste vi skynda oss annars missar vi tåget.
english: Now we must hurry otherwise we miss the train.
tip: skynda sig means to hurry; it needs the reflexive pronoun: vi måste skynda oss.

target: Han skriver långa och detaljerade brev till sin familj.
english: He writes long and detailed letters to his family.
tip: sin means 'his/her own,' pointing back to the subject: skriver brev till sin familj.

target: Jag förstår inte vad du menar med den frågan.
english: I do not understand what you mean with that question.
tip: Inte (not) comes right after the verb in a main clause: Jag förstår inte = I don't understand.

target: Min dotter går i samma skola som ditt barn.
english: My daughter goes to the same school as your child.
tip: Samma paired with som means the same as: samma skola som ditt barn = the same school as your child.

target: De spelar schack mot varandra varje söndag efter middagen.
english: They play chess every Sunday after dinner.
tip: Varandra means each other: spelar schack mot varandra = play chess against one another.

target: Jag lyssnar på svensk musik när jag åker buss.
english: I listen to Swedish music when I ride the bus.
tip: For travel in general drop the article: åker buss = go by bus, versus tar bussen for a specific one.

target: Fönstret i köket går inte att öppna längre tyvärr.
english: The window in the kitchen cannot be opened anymore unfortunately.
tip: Går att means can be done: går inte att öppna = cannot be opened.

target: Flickan hittade ett äpple under det stora trädet igår.
english: The girl found an apple under the big tree yesterday.
tip: A definite noun with an adjective takes a double marker: det stora trädet, both det and -et.

target: Jag läste en intressant artikel i tidningen under lunchen.
english: I read an interesting article in the newspaper during lunch.
tip: under can mean 'during' for a time span: under lunchen = during lunch.

target: Jag arbetar som lärare på en grundskola i Lund.
english: I work as a teacher at an elementary school in Lund.
tip: After som a profession takes no article: arbetar som lärare = work as a teacher.

target: Boken som ligger på bordet tillhör min äldsta syster.
english: The book that lies on the table belongs to my oldest sister.
tip: Gammal is irregular in the superlative: äldsta = oldest, so min äldsta syster.
